data.title: US envoy says Israel has responsibility for Palestinians
data.description: TURMUS AYYA, Palestinian Territories - The US ambassador to Israel said on Saturday that the Israeli government bore responsibility for West Bank Palestinians’ safety and should impose “severe consequences” over violence, as he visited families after a surge in settler attacks.

data.title: Commemoration held for Serbian war criminal Mladic
data.description: BELGRADE - A commemoration was held on Saturday in Belgrade for war criminal Ratko Mladic two days ahead of his burial, attended by dozens of former military personnel, family members and officials.

data.title: Russia hits Kyiv airports as Trump envoys awaited
data.description: KYIV - Russian strikes hit Kyiv’s airports overnight, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday, as US envoys arrived in Moscow to discuss a plan to end more than four years of war.

data.title: Global autonomous weapons pact taking shape
data.description: GENEVA - The ⁠128 ⁠states party to ​a framework that regulates or bans weapons considered as indiscriminate, ​or causing too many ‌injuries, have agreed on a document that could pave the way to international rules on autonomous weapons.

data.title: Masked anti-migrant protesters shut down UK port
data.description: Dozens of masked people reportedly protesting against Channel migrant crossings blocked access to the Port of Dover in southern England on Saturday, halting traffic that is ferried between France and the UK.

data.title: Nepal tunnel rescue revives hope 10 days after flood
data.description: KATHMANDU - Rescuers in Nepal pulled a Chinese man out alive on Saturday from a tunnel buried by debris, as emergency response teams dug with new vigour in the search for missing people 10 days after catastrophic flooding.

data.title: More orangutans rescued from Indonesian wildfire
data.description: JAKARTA - An orangutan mother and her baby, threatened by encroaching wildfires to their habitat in Indonesia, were rescued earlier this week, authorities said on Saturday.

data.title: The poet, the grave and the grocer: an Icelandic mystery
data.description: THINGVELLIR, Iceland - In a small enclosure of lava stones in a grassy field, a modest tombstone bears the name of an Icelandic legend: Jonas Hallgrimsson. But are the bones beneath it really those of the poet, or a Danish grocer?

data.title: Haze from Indonesian fires spreading again
data.description: JAKARTA - Thick smog has blanketed parts of Indonesia as the vast archipelago battles to contain fires that have burned large swathes of Borneo and Sumatra.

data.title: Bolivian army base blasts kill two, wound dozens
data.description: VIACHA, Bolivia - Two explosions at an army barracks in Bolivia killed at least two people and wounded 81 on Friday, authorities said.

data.title: Srebrenica: A massacre that outraged the world
data.description: SARAJEVO - Srebrenica became a symbol of ethnic cleansing after its men and boys were massacred by Bosnian Serbs following a three-year-long siege during the Balkan wars of the 1990s.

data.title: US envoys take new peace plan to Moscow and Kyiv
data.description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump said on Friday he is sending envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv with a plan to end more than four years of war in Ukraine.

data.title: Africa bigger, US smaller - UN adopts new map
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - The United Nations General Assembly voted Friday to adopt a new world map that makes the African continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe, drawing ire from Washington.

data.title: Trump sends envoys to Moscow, Kyiv with new plan to 'end war'
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Friday he is sending envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv with a plan to end more than four years of war in Ukraine.

data.title: WHO says key warehouse destroyed by attack in Ukraine
data.description: GENEVA - The World Health Organization said Friday that one of its main warehouses in Ukraine had been destroyed in air attack -- the third such incident in three months.

data.title: 5 EU countries aim to send rejected migrants to 'return hub' by 2027
data.description: COPENHAGEN - Five EU countries are seeking a deal with a country outside the bloc to host a "return hub" for migrants whose asylum applications have been rejected, with a targeted start date of January 1, a Danish minister said Friday.

data.title: Trump says envoys taking plan to 'end the war' to Moscow, Kyiv
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Friday that he was sending envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to Moscow and Kyiv with a proposal to end the four-year-old Ukraine war.

data.title: More than 120 killed in Yemen's worst clashes in years: sources
data.description: SANAA - A major offensive by Yemen's Houthis to seize control of the gateway to the Red Sea has left more than 120 people dead, sources told AFP Friday, the country's deadliest clashes in years.

data.title: Call to ‘turn off the tap’ to Ukraine sparks furore in France
data.description: PARIS - A senior official in French presidential contender Marine Le Pen’s far-right party sparked a furore on Friday with a comment that France would “turn off the tap” to Ukraine if it came to power.

data.title: Voting begins in crucial US midterm elections
data.description: WASHINGTON - Voting in the US midterm elections effectively began Friday as North Carolina became the first state to send out mail ballots for contests expected to threaten President Donald Trump’s Republican control of Congress.

data.title: France to abandon ‘distorted’ Mercator map projection
data.description: PARIS - The French foreign ministry on Friday said it plans to abandon using maps with the traditional Mercator projection of the world, backing a push by Africa to give the continent a more realistic geographical representation.

data.title: Swiss far-right extremists go on trial amid protests
data.description: ZURICH - Six members of the Swiss far-right Junge Tat movement went on trial in Zurich on Friday on charges including inciting hatred in disrupting LGBTQ events, as protesters rallied outside calling for their conviction.

data.title: Rubio to visit Trump-friendly allies in South America
data.description: WASHINGTON - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel next week to Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, three Latin American nations whose leaders are close to President Donald Trump, the State Department said Friday.

data.title: Weather and war push up world food prices
data.description: PARIS - Food price inflation accelerated in August as drought and conflicts impacted commodity markets, with sugar prices hitting their highest level in more than a year, UN data showed on Friday.
